option_a_keep_original_v2.strategy: Retain Original Supervisor V2 exclusively in production; keep Vocabulary Guidance V1 purely within offline benchmark suites.
option_a_keep_original_v2.pros: Zero production risk; zero changes to prompt registry or runtime configuration.
option_a_keep_original_v2.cons: Forfeits the observed +37.5pp canonical validity gain for developers opting into structured integration testing.

option_b_prepare_experimental_opt_in.strategy: Prepare an explicit, non-default configuration toggle (agent_enable_vocabulary_guidance=False by default) allowing developers to opt-in to Guidance V1.
option_b_prepare_experimental_opt_in.pros: Safely bridges benchmark discoveries to developer workflows without risking production default safety; enforces audit logging of prompt versions and guidance hashes.
option_b_prepare_experimental_opt_in.cons: Requires adding a settings flag and documenting experimental boundaries.

option_c_research_guidance_v2.strategy: Iterate prompt engineering to formulate Guidance V2 specifically addressing cross-system identity overreach (F3 failure mode).
option_c_research_guidance_v2.pros: Directly targets the remaining semantic defect identified in RCA-2A.12/13.
option_c_research_guidance_v2.cons: Risks ad-hoc prompt overfitting on development fixtures if pursued prior to real orchestrator integration.

decision_rationale: Vocabulary Guidance V1 showed a +37.5pp canonical validity advantage in RCA-2A.12, but suffered cross-system identity overreach in F3. It cannot be made production default. However, locking it away completely in benchmarks prevents developers from benefiting from improved integration formatting. Preparing an explicit opt-in toggle (defaulting to False) represents the soundest engineering compromise.
